stories.headline: West Bengal Assembly Elections 2026: BJP-TMC battle intensifies ahead of Phase 2 vote
stories.summary: With Phase 2 polling scheduled for April 29, BJP leaders Modi and Shah conducted intensive campaigning across West Bengal, claiming a decisive win from Phase 1's record ~93% turnout. Modi held rallies invoking women's safety and the RG Kar case, while Shah predicted BJP would win 110 of 152 Phase 1 seats and promised UCC, end of 'syndicate raj,' and a Bengali BJP chief minister; TMC's Mamata Banerjee countered with legal threats against Shah and her own seat projections. Violence between BJP and TMC workers also flared ahead of Modi's visits.

stories.headline: Trump's 'hellhole' remark about India sparks diplomatic rebuke and opposition attacks on Modi's silence
stories.summary: US President Trump shared a social media post featuring a podcast host's remarks calling India a 'hellhole' and accusing Indian immigrants of abusing birthright citizenship. India's foreign ministry spokesperson called the remarks 'uninformed, inappropriate and in poor taste,' while the opposition Congress and other parties used the episode to attack Modi for his silence and alleged inability to push back on his 'friend' Trump.

stories.headline: Raghav Chadha leads seven AAP Rajya Sabha MPs in mass defection to BJP
stories.summary: AAP's Raghav Chadha announced on April 24 that he and six other AAP Rajya Sabha MPs—including Sandeep Pathak, Swati Maliwal, Harbhajan Singh, Ashok Mittal, Rajendra Gupta, and Vikram Sahney—would merge with the BJP, invoking the anti-defection clause's two-thirds merger exception. The defection, which the AAP called 'Operation Lotus,' follows internal tensions after Chadha was removed as deputy leader; legal experts questioned its constitutional validity.

stories.headline: Former Army Chief Naravane breaks silence on memoir controversy, releases new book on military history
stories.summary: Former Army Chief General MM Naravane spoke publicly about the controversy surrounding his unpublished memoir 'Four Stars of Destiny,' calling it 'unwarranted' and 'unfair' to drag the forces into political debate. He reiterated that 'not an inch' of territory was lost to China during the 2020 Ladakh standoff, stressed the importance of keeping the armed forces apolitical, and launched a new book 'The Curious and the Classified' on Indian military myths and traditions.

stories.headline: NSA Doval conducts Gulf outreach: visits Saudi Arabia then UAE to discuss energy security and West Asia situation
stories.summary: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval visited Saudi Arabia (around April 19-20) and then UAE (April 26-27), meeting senior leaders including UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi. Discussions focused on strengthening strategic partnerships, energy security given ongoing West Asia conflict, and regional stability. The back-to-back visits followed EAM Jaishankar's earlier UAE tour, signaling intensive Indian outreach to Gulf partners.

stories.headline: RBI cancels Paytm Payments Bank licence; new digital payment authentication rules issued
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India cancelled the banking licence of Paytm Payments Bank Limited on April 24 citing governance lapses and regulatory violations, prompting the bank's board to approve winding-up proceedings. Separately, the RBI issued a comprehensive new e-mandate framework requiring additional authentication for recurring digital payments over ₹15,000 and issued related regulatory guidance on card issuers and auto-debit rules. The RBI's deputy governor also reaffirmed that recent rupee support measures are temporary.

stories.headline: Modi to address India's global envoys on April 30 as Heads of Mission conference focuses on West Asia, Iran war
stories.summary: India is convening a Heads of Mission conference at which Prime Minister Modi will address Indian diplomats on April 30, joined by EAM Jaishankar, NSA Doval, and CDS Chauhan. Jaishankar will brief envoys on the new global order shaped by the Iran war, West Asia conflict, Ukraine, and China's growing influence. The Strait of Hormuz disruption is a central agenda item given India's energy and trade exposure.

stories.headline: India-UK Strategic Dialogue: Jaishankar and Doval hold back-to-back meetings with UK NSA Powell
stories.summary: UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell visited New Delhi for the annual India-UK Strategic Dialogue, holding separate meetings with EAM Jaishankar and NSA Doval. Discussions covered regional and global security issues, defence cooperation, counter-terrorism, maritime security, and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries.

stories.headline: UNGA President Baerbock to visit India on April 28 for multilateral talks and AI governance session
stories.summary: Annalena Baerbock, President of the 80th session of the UN General Assembly, will visit India on April 28 at EAM Jaishankar's invitation. She will discuss multilateral issues, pay homage at Rajghat, and attend an AI governance session with MEITY. This is the second high-level German diplomatic contact with Jaishankar in the context of her new role.

stories.headline: NSA Doval meets Muslim community leaders with 'we sail or sink together' national unity message
stories.summary: NSA Ajit Doval held a meeting at the PMO Building with approximately 14 eminent Muslims including industrialists, educationists, activists, a doctor, and a journalist. Doval emphasized national unity using the metaphor of India as a 'large ship,' noted rising Muslim recruitment in the armed forces, and encouraged community leaders to engage proactively with national development goals.

stories.headline: Modi expresses relief after White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting evacuation of Trump
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi issued a statement on social media expressing relief that US President Trump, First Lady Melania Trump, and Vice President JD Vance were safe after a shooting incident forced an evacuation at the White House Correspondents' Dinner. Modi stated that 'violence has no place in a democracy' and must be 'unequivocally condemned.'
